why: wish + past for now is on the B2.2 card; the task is already a learning task (role learn), so easy is fine. *I wish I would live* is the card's own listed mistake (*I wish I would have more time*), so it is believable.

why: Gate long_frame: the speech frame is a setting in front of the instruction, but it is what rules out *If only we listened* (a present-habit reading). The frame goes and *last year ... now* in the sentence does its job; *had listen* (a form nobody chooses) is dropped.

wrong: If only we would have listened to the warning signs last year, we would not be in this position now.

fix.why_lv: *If only* + *had* + 3. forma izsaka nožēlu par pagātni (*last year*), tad *would* + pamatforma rezultātam tagad. Nav pareizi *would have listened*, un arī *listened*, kas attiecas uz tagadni.

The instruction is unnatural and gives the start and the end away (rule: a word order says only *Put the words in order.*). Without it the other natural orders (*if*-part second, *now* before *a doctor*) must be accepted.

answers: if I had studied medicine I would be a doctor now
if I had studied medicine I would now be a doctor
I would be a doctor now if I had studied medicine

fix.why: *If I had studied* imagines a different past decision; *I would be a doctor now* is the result now. *now* can also stand before *a doctor*, and the *if*-part can come second.
